title: Adhyaya 6: Classical Duties & Dharma
summary: Canonical verses on traditional righteousness from Adhyaya 6.
ai_summary: Exposition of ethical conduct and cosmic law according to Sage Manu in Adhyaya 6.

verses.original: धृतिः क्षमा दमोऽस्तेयं शौचमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः । धीर्विद्या सत्यमक्रोधो दशकं धर्मलक्षणम् ॥
verses.transliteration: dhṛtiḥ kṣamā damo'steyaṁ śaucamindriyanigrahaḥ | dhīrvidyā satyamakrodho daśakaṁ dharmalakṣaṇam ||
verses.translation: Steadfast fortitude (Dhriti), forgiveness (Kshama), self-control (Dama), non-stealing (Asteya), purity (Shaucha), mastery of senses (Indriya-nigraha), wisdom (Dhi), spiritual knowledge (Vidya), truthfulness (Satya), and absence of anger (Akrodha) — these ten constitute the marks of Dharma.

layers.author: medhatithi
layers.content: The celebrated ten universal virtues of character that define ethical human life regardless of social station.

layers.author: kulluka-bhatta
layers.content: कुल्लूक भट्ट भाष्य: Steadfast fortitude (Dhriti), forgiveness (Kshama), self-control (Dama), non-stealing (Asteya), purity (Shaucha), mastery of senses (Indriya-nigraha), wisdom (Dhi), spiritual knowledge (Vidya), truthfulness (Satya), and absence of anger (Akrodha) — these ten constitute the marks of Dharma.

layers.author: buhler
layers.author_label: Sacred Books of the East Vol 25
layers.content: मनुस्मृती अध्याय 6: The celebrated ten universal virtues of character that define ethical human life regardless of social station.

verses.original: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । संपश्यन्नात्मयाजी वै स्वाराज्यमधिगच्छति ॥
verses.transliteration: sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṁ sarvabhūtāni cātmani | saṁpaśyannātmayājī vai svārājyamadhigacchati ||
verses.translation: He who beholds the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, offering the sacrifice of the Self, attains supreme self-sovereignty.

layers.author: medhatithi
layers.content: The peak Vedantic realization enshrined at the climax of the hermit and renunciant stages.

layers.author: kulluka-bhatta
layers.content: कुल्लूक भट्ट भाष्य: He who beholds the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self, offering the sacrifice of the Self, attains supreme self-sovereignty.
